title: Partition route failures without hiding data integrity errors
businessContext: A notification outage turns every account page into a blank loading screen indefinitely.
problemStatement: Design the system for Dashboard with billing, reports and notifications; dependencies have independent SLOs. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Define which partial failures are tolerable.
Preserve error ownership, retry and cancellation.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: Dashboard with billing, reports and notifications; dependencies have independent SLOs
functional: Define which partial failures are tolerable.
Preserve error ownership, retry and cancellation.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Place Suspense/error boundaries around independently valuable subtrees below shared layouts, and start independent work without a parent waterfall.

A fallback can hide an endless request and make a broken page appear merely slow. Track pending age and terminal outcomes, propagate cancellation and alert on sustained failure rather than leaving unbounded spinners.
alternativeApproaches: No. It is a promise-composition tool, not an ownership or UX policy. Decide which partial results are safe and useful, then choose boundaries and response handling that express that decision.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Fail each dependency independently and in combinations.
Retry after recovery without losing unrelated client state.
Test navigation/account changes while old requests remain in flight.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
